description: Evidence requirements. All evidence is live: read from GitHub, git, or command output at task time. Missing evidence resolves to the listed status, naming exactly what is missing.

entries.satisfied_by: The current GitHub issue or PR defining objective, scope, out of scope, and acceptance criteria, read live.
Links to the prior issues, PRs, ADRs, or decisions the current task builds on, cited in the issue or gathered live.
Real command output showing current branch, worktree status, and HEAD, captured before the first edit.
Live git/GitHub reads of the files, branches, diffs, or history the task depends on.

Exact scoped PM approval naming the repository, the issue or PR, and the approved action or command bundle, in the current conversation or recorded on the issue/PR. Explicit PM decisions are evidence for the point decided per execution_modes approval_note.
The validation commands run for this change with their real results (tests, linters, type checks, kernel validation, or the project's documented checks).
entries.notes: Done is never claimed without this evidence reported.

entries.satisfied_by: The PR's real changed-file list and diff, plus relevant final head file content when the diff alone is insufficient to understand behavior. PR body, comments, terminal-agent reports, and validation summaries are claims or evidence leads, not proof of implementation. If this code evidence cannot be inspected, use status.needs_context instead of GO.
Review findings or verdict recorded on the PR or issue.
A closure comment with completion evidence, validation evidence with output, boundaries preserved, and commit/PR references, per the traceability protocol.

For target-project adoption: target repository identity; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md/browser-chat adapter presence; existing adapter metadata, roadmap anchor, kernel repo/path/version, project notes, validation commands, durable live-state risk, and audit findings from KERNEL_REPOSITORY templates or tools.audit_target_adapters, read live.

Live confirmation that one named, approved internal environment is ready to deploy: the exact deploy commands are documented as target-owned in the target's Project-specific notes (never invented), the environment scope (local or staging) is named and separately approved, prerequisite build/migration/config steps are validated, and secret-safety is confirmed by naming only variables, command names, file paths, and risk types, never values.
entries.notes: Deployment fails closed hard. Missing or ambiguous readiness, missing target-owned commands, missing environment scope, or unconfirmed secret-safety blocks execution. Production readiness is stricter, stays with the Human PM by default, and is not satisfied by this evidence for a terminal agent.
